title: PROJEXA Universal AI Work Link - capability matrix
revision: LINK-FIX 2026-09-25: audit S02 defects A-04 (identity marks), A-14 (Claude in Chrome L6) and A-23 (R-file labels on every cell; surface confidence = lowest cell; FETCHED-S01 re-fetched, see AILINK_S01_fetches.md)
evidence_note: Every cell carries `label` (the AILINK_Rnn file's own confidence label and section, carried over unchanged: R01 FETCHED / FETCHED via relay / PARTLY; R02 FETCHED-SUMMARY / SEARCH-ONLY; R03 FETCHED / SEARCH; R04 FETCHED via summariser / SEARCH-ONLY; R05 VERIFIED_FETCHED / PARTLY_VERIFIED; R06 FETCHED / SEARCH-ONLY / THIRD-PARTY; R07 FETCHED / SEARCH-ONLY (team blog and community pages are not product documentation); R08 FETCHED / FETCHED-3P / SEARCH-ONLY / summariser negatives; R09 FETCHED / SEARCH-ONLY / THIRD-PARTY / INFERENCE; S01 = our own design or an inference with no R-file line) and `confidence` on one scale: VERIFIED_FETCHED > PARTLY_VERIFIED > UNVERIFIED, or DESIGN for our own layer statements. FETCHED-S01 facts were re-fetched 2026-09-25 (AILINK_S01_fetches.md).

layers.L1_markdown_get: A plain GET of the pasted link returns the Markdown manual; every read is a further GET whose absolute URL is printed in the manual.
layers.L2_openapi_import: The AI tool imports /openapi.json (3.0.3) or /swagger.json (2.0); header mode /...?mode=header with Link-Token for tools that store a key.
layers.L3_mcp: The same link used as a remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no authentication, both MCP eras), or header mode F/header with Link-Token / Bearer.
layers.L4_http_by_client: The AI or the code around it sends its own GET and POST requests (shell curl, client-executed function calling).
layers.L5_get_propose_confirm: The AI opens /propose?fn=..&p.x=.. (stateless GET) and hands the returned confirm link to the person, who clicks Confirm on the static page.
layers.L6_paste_back: Token-free paste card (+ token-free data file) given to the AI; the AI returns projexa-proposal blocks; the person pastes them into the inbox page.
layers.L7_email_inbound: The person emails proposal blocks to a per-link inbound address. Future layer: needs owner DNS/MX (work order Q4).

values.zero_setup: Works from the pasted link or pasted card with only the AI's own normal sign-in.
values.zero_setup_per_call_approval: No configuration, but the AI tool asks a human to approve each call (e.g. a shell command).
values.human_opens_link: The person opens the link in a browser tab; the AI reads that tab or clicks the page like a person.
values.one_time_user_setup: NOT zero setup: the person adds the link once (connector form or config file).
values.admin_or_maker_setup: NOT zero setup: a workspace admin, org owner or maker must add it.
values.developer_code: NOT zero setup: needs code written around the model and the developer's own API key.
values.not_available: Documented or observed as absent for this surface.
values.not_applicable: The layer has no meaning for this surface (for example no human in the loop).
values.unverified: No fetched page or test settles it; the named owner test decides it.
values.future_owner_dns: Designed but not built; needs an owner DNS/MX action first.

uniformity_verdict: One pasted URL is a uniform ENTRY POINT for all nine families (manual, or paste card + inbox page through the person). It is NOT uniform zero-setup machine access: documented zero-setup readers are Claude web fetch (API rule; claude.ai chat pending OT-05), Claude Code, Gemini CLI, browser sidebars via an open tab, and developer APIs; ChatGPT, Gemini app, consumer Copilot, workplace Copilot Chat and chat.z.ai are UNVERIFIED (owner tests); DeepSeek chat and email AIs cannot read the URL. Every MCP/OpenAPI path needs a one-time click by the user or an admin. Connectors that an admin, owner or maker installs for several people are refused for per-user links (T20, OT-18).
confidence_rule: A surface's `confidence` is the LOWEST `confidence` of its seven cells, DESIGN cells left out (audit A-23, V-13). Most surfaces are UNVERIFIED for that reason: at least one layer is unknown.
identity_rule: A link acts as exactly one person. `shared_identity_risk: true` marks a cell where the vendor's setup puts one key or URL in front of several people (admin, owner, maker or project-wide install). Such a cell has `allowed_for_per_user_link: false`: the manual refuses it (threat T20) until owner test OT-18 shows a second person's call through it is refused or recorded as that second person (audit A-04, PMD-26).
